subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What is the size of each exterior angle of a regular hexagon?
questions.explain: Exterior angles sum to 360°, so each is 360° ÷ 6 = 60°.

questions.q: tan x = 1, where x is between 0° and 90°. What is the angle x?
Each interior angle of a regular polygon is 150 deg. How many sides does it have?
questions.explain: Each exterior angle = 180 - 150 = 30 deg, so sides = 360 / 30 = 12.

questions.q: Co-interior (allied) angles between parallel lines: one is 130°. What is the other?
A line drawn from the centre of a circle to a point on the circumference is called the:
questions.explain: A radius joins the centre to the circumference.

questions.q: The bearing of Q from P is 210 deg. What is the bearing of P from Q?
questions.explain: Since 210 is more than 180, subtract: 210 - 180 = 030 deg.

questions.q: Two angles are vertically opposite. One is 47°. What is the other?
questions.explain: Vertically opposite angles are equal, so it is 47°.

A prism has cross-sectional area 12 cm^2 and length 7 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explain: Volume of a prism = cross-sectional area × length = 12 × 7 = 84 cm^3.

questions.q: A circle has circumference 31.4 cm. What is its radius? (Use pi = 3.14)
A closed cylinder has radius 2 cm and height 5 cm. What is its total surface area? (Use pi = 3.14)
Three angles meet at a point and are 120°, 150° and x. What is x?
questions.explain: Angles around a point sum to 360°, so x = 360° − 120° − 150° = 90°.

questions.q: You walk from a point on a bearing of 270°. In which direction are you walking?
questions.explain: A bearing of 270° measured clockwise from North points due West.

questions.q: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is 112 deg. What is its corresponding angle?
questions.explain: Corresponding (F) angles are equal, so it is 112 deg.
